comments.text:
I remember my mum renting this exact film from Blockbuster when I was about six. TerrorVision came out in ’86, so I must’ve watched it a couple of years later — probably shoved on the low shelf where little kids could grab it and permanently damage themselves. 
She stuck it on, then buggered off next door for tea and gossip for three hours. She must’ve read the back of the box and thought ‘yeah, he’ll be fine’.
I was NOT fine.  
This thing was eating people, wearing their heads like puppets, chatting through tentacles… absolutely traumatised me. No happy ending either  the kid’s gone, the sister’s gone, everyone’s doomed. Proper early lesson that children are not safe in the universe.
Watching it again years later and suddenly clocking the swingers, the punk with the wrist thing, the monster thinking he’s its owner until he gives it a slap and it goes full man‑devouring rage… plus that granddad with the bunker and enough machine guns to invade Belgium what a wild, bizarre masterpiece. 
Honestly, films today could never. They’d just CGI the life out of it and throw in a couple of blue Avatar extras doing parkour on the satellite.
